name: LATHE
expansion: Latent Activation Topology of Hidden Embeddings

intro.problem: The hidden layers of the classifiers used in long-lived-particle searches are rarely examined, and we do not yet know whether visualizing them is merely striking or genuinely useful, for instance as an n-dimensional heat map showing where in latent space background closure succeeds and fails.
intro.value: If it is useful, latent maps could diagnose failures, separate training objectives that score alike, guide architecture choices in TRUSS, and tie what a network learned back to physical inputs, as related work has begun to do for jet taggers [@khot2023][@komiske2020].
intro.approach: We treat this as exploration with an exit: map trained models in prediction space [@mao2024], compare their hidden layers [@kornblith2019][@davari2023], and trace training trajectories [@horoi2022], then run a pre-registered kill test asking whether map coordinates predict held-out closure better than hyperparameters alone.
intro.goals: The outcome is an honest verdict. If the kill test passes, an interactive explorer whose structures are stable across seeds becomes an analysis tool; if it fails, we record that the latent picture adds nothing a metrics table does not, and stop.

questions: Is a latent map useful at all, or only striking: does it predict anything a metrics table does not?
Could an n-dimensional heat map of closure over latent space show where and why the background estimate fails?
Which latent structures survive across seeds, and which are artifacts of the projection?

components.name: First attempts
components.subtitle: What gets built and run first
components.summary: Small, cheap probes chosen so that a negative answer arrives quickly. Each one reuses models that already exist or come out of the baseline re-run.

items.label: Probe set
items.detail: Carve out held-out events before cross-validation so every model is compared on data none of them trained on

items.label: Model space
items.detail: One point per trained model, distances from per-event predicted probabilities, embedded the way the training-manifold work does [@mao2024][@klabunde2025]

items.label: Event space
items.detail: Hidden-layer activations of a single model, compared across seeds and objectives with CKA and its known failure modes guarded [@kornblith2019][@davari2023]

items.label: Positive control
items.detail: A known change in training regime along the decorrelation sweep should show up as a kink in the model-space trajectory; if it does not, the map is not seeing real structure

items.label: Dead-unit census
items.detail: Count hidden units that never activate, which also feeds the connection sizing in TRUSS [@khot2023]

components.name: The heat-map idea
components.subtitle: Where this could become useful
components.summary: Color latent space by background closure, signal density, or per-event contribution to the closure error, so regions where the ABCD estimate breaks down become visible. This is the version of the idea that could earn its keep; it is not yet known whether such regions exist.

items.label: Intrinsic dimension
items.detail: Measure how many directions the representation actually uses before mapping it, with shuffled and untrained controls [@ansuini2019]

items.label: Stability
items.detail: Display only structures that persist across seeds and projection choices; mode connectivity tests whether two solutions are really distinct [@garipov2018]

components.name: Kill test
components.subtitle: Pre-registered exit
components.summary: Before anything is built into a tool, test whether map-derived quantities predict closure on held-out events better than the training hyperparameters alone. If they do not, the project stops with that result written down.

links.title: Architecture search
links.text: If latent maps prove useful, their features become an input to TRUSS's architecture generation; the dead-unit census feeds its connection sizing either way.
